title: How does the power line of four help us calculate?
description: The power line of four is used to work out two divisions and a multiplication of big numbers by moving along the line. All three land on the same power of four. Keeko doubts whether the exponents are multiplied or added.
teaching_notes: One idea: on a power line, multiplying moves right and dividing moves left, so the exponents are added or taken away. Watch for students who multiply the exponents, or who move the wrong way along the line when dividing.

source: Use the power line of 4 to find 65536 ÷ 64, 64 × 16 and 16384 ÷ 16 as powers of 4.
video_script.why: A learner sees that moving along a power line is the same as adding or taking away exponents.
video_script.substitution: the book's own power line of four and its three calculations
video_script.anchor: the power line of four, from four to the power one to four to the power eight, drawn on the board
video_script.wrong_move: multiplies the exponents three and two instead of adding them
video_script.payoff_line: Dividing moves left on the power line, and multiplying moves right

final_answer.value: All three are 4 to the power 5, which is 1024
final_answer.spoken: all three are four to the power five, which is one thousand and twenty four

maths_rules: dividing by 4^2 is multiplying by 4^-2: 4^7 x 4^-2 = 4^5
video_script.design: One idea: moving along the power line adds or takes away exponents. Wrong idea: multiply the exponents. The power line is drawn with the 4^5 spot left empty, and the three moves land there before the number is written at the answer.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the power line of 4 with three calculations below it and a question mark

marks.line: the power line of 4 is drawn from 4^1 to 4^8
marks.ask: a question mark glows beside the three calculations

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='line'/>The book gives a power line of four.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Use it to find sixty five thousand five hundred and thirty six divided by sixty four.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Then sixty four times sixteen.
<bookmark mark='three'/>Then sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four divided by sixteen.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Can you write each as a power of four?

beats.on_screen: the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.line: the powers of 4 are marked in order, with the spot for 4^5 left blank
marks.right: an arrow to the right is labelled times 4 for each step
marks.left: an arrow to the left is labelled divide by 4 for each step

narration: <bookmark mark='line'/>A power line lists the powers of one number in order.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Each step to the right multiplies by four.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Each step to the left divides by four.

beats.on_screen: Given: the power line of 4; 65536 / 64, 64 x 16, 16384 / 16

marks.given: the three calculations are written under the power line

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the power line of four, and three calculations.

beats.on_screen: To find: each answer as a power of 4

marks.find: the words each answer as a power of 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each answer as a power of four.

marks.find: 65536 is found at 4^8 and 64 at 4^3 on the line
marks.left: an arrow moves 3 places left from 4^8, landing at 4^5

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>Step one, take sixty five thousand five hundred and thirty six divided by sixty four.
<bookmark mark='left'/>On the line, they sit at four to the power eight, and four cubed. Dividing moves left three places.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Eight take away three gives five.

marks.find: 64 is found at 4^3 and 16 at 4^2 on the line
marks.right: an arrow moves 2 places right from 4^3, landing at 4^5

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>Step two, take sixty four times sixteen. Sixty four is four cubed, and sixteen is four squared.
<bookmark mark='right'/>Multiplying moves right two places.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Three plus two gives five.

marks.find: 16384 is found at 4^7 and 16 at 4^2 on the line
marks.left: an arrow moves 2 places left from 4^7, landing at 4^5

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>Step three, take sixteen thousand three hundred and eighty four divided by sixteen. These sit at four to the power seven, and four squared.
<bookmark mark='left'/>Dividing moves left two places.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Seven take away two gives five.

beats.on_screen: dividing by 4^2 is the same as multiplying by 4^-2: 4^7 x 4^-2 = 4^(7 + (-2)) = 4^5

marks.neg: 4^7 x 4^-2 is written beside the third calculation

narration: <bookmark mark='neg'/>Step four, dividing by sixteen is the same as multiplying by four to the power negative two.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Seven plus negative two is five, so it lands on four to the power five again.

marks.pay: the left and right arrows are boxed
marks.ans: 4^5 is boxed on the line and 4^5 = 1024 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>Dividing moves left on the power line, and multiplying moves right.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>All three are four to the power five, which is one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Sixty four times sixteen does give one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 64 x 16 = 4^(3 x 2) = 4^6, struck out; 4^6 = 4096 beside it

marks.all: the bubble is struck out and 3 + 2 = 5 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks sixty four times sixteen is four to the power six. Keeko multiplied three and two.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But four to the power six is four thousand and ninety six. That is far more than one thousand and twenty four.
<bookmark mark='all'/>On the power line, multiplying adds the exponents, so three plus two is five.
